hello.note: Works at any time of day, often with palms pressed together. नमस्ते (namaste) is also used.

goodbye.note: Lit. 'I'll come (again)': Marathi avoids saying 'I'm going'. A woman says: येते (yete).

please.note: Formal. In speech, politeness comes from the verb form or a soft ना: बसा ना (basa na).

thank_you.note: More formal: मी आभारी आहे (mi aabhaari aahe). Many people simply say थँक यू (thank you).

youre_welcome.note: Marathi has no set reply to thanks; this ('oh, it's nothing') is the natural one.

yes.note: Also होय (hoy), the fuller form: a little more formal, and the one used in writing.

no.note: To turn down an offer, say नको (nako), 'I don't want it'.

excuse_me.note: People also call strangers दादा (daada, 'brother') or ताई (taai, 'sister'). In cities: एक्सक्यूज मी (excuse me).

good_morning.note: Formal or in messages. Face to face, most people say नमस्कार (namaskaar) or गुड मॉर्निंग (good morning).

how_are_you.note: To a woman: तुम्ही कशा आहात? (tumhi kasha aahat?). Casual: कसं काय? (kasa kaay?)

im_fine.note: A woman says: मी बरी आहे (mi bari aahe). Also common: मी मजेत आहे (mi majet aahe).

whats_your_name.note: More formal: आपलं नाव काय? (aapla naav kaay?)

my_name_is.note: The verb आहे (aahe, 'is') comes last, after the name.

where_from.note: To a woman: तुम्ही कुठल्या आहात? (tumhi kuthlya aahat?)

im_from.note: A woman says: मी …ची आहे (mi …chi aahe). The place name changes form: पुणे → पुण्याचा (Pune → Punyaacha).

speak_english.note: Lit. 'Does English come to you?' Many say इंग्लिश (English) instead of इंग्रजी.

dont_understand.note: Also common: मला कळलं नाही (mala kalla naahi).

speak_slowly.note: More direct: कृपया हळू बोला (krupaya halu bola).

what.note: To ask someone to repeat, politer: काय म्हणालात? (kaay mhanaalaat?)

why.note: The same word ends yes/no questions: येतं का? (yeta ka?). Also common: कशाला? (kashaala?, 'what for?')

how_much.note: For the total at the till: किती झाले? (kiti jhaale?)

where_bathroom.note: Also common: बाथरूम (bathroom). Signs say स्वच्छतागृह (swachchhataagruh) or शौचालय (shauchaalay).

what_time.note: The answer uses the same verb: दोन वाजले (don vaajle), 'it's two o'clock'.

four.note: Marathi digit: ४. Here च sounds like 'ts': tsaar.

five.note: Marathi digit: ५. The final च sounds like 'ts': paats.

eight.note: Marathi digit: ८. ठ is a tongue-curled t with a puff of air, not English 'th'.

water.note: ण is a retroflex n: curl the tongue back to say it.

tea.note: Here च sounds like 'ts': tsaha. It comes with milk and sugar unless you ask otherwise.

bread.note: Soft bread rolls, as in वडापाव (vadapaav). Sliced bread: ब्रेड (bread). Flatbread: पोळी (poli).

menu_please.note: जरा (jara, 'a little') softens a request, much like 'please'.

delicious.note: Said of food that has 'turned out' well. Casual: एकदम मस्त! (ekdam mast!) The word for tasty: चविष्ट (chavisht).

no_meat.note: Also: मी शाकाहारी आहे (mi shaakaahaari aahe), 'I'm vegetarian'.

enjoy_meal.note: Marathi has no fixed 'bon appétit'; hosts say this, lit. 'eat unhurriedly'.

left.note: Turn left: डावीकडे वळा (daavikade vala). Drivers also say लेफ्ट (left).

right.note: Turn right: उजवीकडे वळा (ujvikade vala). Drivers also say राइट (right).

stop_here.note: Softer, to a driver: दादा, इथे थांबवा ना (daada, ithe thaambva na).

airport.note: In everyday speech most people say एअरपोर्ट (airport).

hotel.note: In Maharashtra हॉटेल often means a restaurant or eatery, too.

train_station.note: Often just स्टेशन (station). Signs say रेल्वे स्थानक (railway sthaanak).

want_to_go.note: The place takes -ला ('to'): मला पुण्याला जायचं आहे (mala Punyaala jaaycha aahe).

is_it_far.note: How far is it? किती लांब आहे? (kiti laamb aahe?)

one_ticket.note: Name the place first: पुण्याचं एक तिकीट द्या (Punyaacha ek ticket dya).

too_expensive.note: When bargaining, add: जरा कमी करा ना (jara kami kara na), 'bring it down a bit'.

cheaper.note: Also: जरा स्वस्त दाखवा (jara swast daakhva), 'show me something cheaper'.

id_like_this.note: Also common: मला हे पाहिजे (mala he paahije). At the counter: हे द्या (he dya).

just_looking.note: A woman says: मी फक्त बघतेय (mi fakt baghtey).

pay_card.note: Handy pattern for anything: कॅश चालेल का? (cash chaalel ka?), 'is cash OK?'

cash.note: In everyday speech कॅश (cash) is just as common.

open.note: In speech: दुकान चालू आहे (dukaan chaalu aahe), 'the shop is open'.

closed.note: Rhymes with 'fund'. Also means 'switched off', for lights, phones and so on.

big.note: With feminine nouns: मोठी (mothi); with neuter ones: मोठं (motha, with a light nasal).

small.note: Same form for every gender. Also common: छोटा (chhota).

good_evening.note: Formal or in messages. Face to face, people just say नमस्कार (namaskaar).

good_night.note: In everyday speech also गुड नाइट (good night).

see_you_later.note: Also: पुन्हा भेटू (punha bhetu), 'see you again'.

need_doctor.note: Also: डॉक्टरला बोलवा (doctorla bolva), 'please call a doctor'.

im_lost.note: A woman says: मी रस्ता चुकले आहे (mi rasta chukle aahe).

dont_feel_well.note: Also: माझी तब्येत बरी नाही (maajhi tabyet bari naahi).

pharmacy.note: In everyday speech people say मेडिकल (medical) or केमिस्ट (chemist).

hospital.note: In speech most say हॉस्पिटल (hospital). A local clinic is a दवाखाना (davaakhaana).

lost_phone.note: If it was stolen: माझा फोन चोरीला गेला (maajha phone chorila gela).

allergic.note: The allergen takes -ची: मला दुधाची ॲलर्जी आहे (mala dudhaachi allergy aahe), 'to milk'.

be_careful.note: Also: जपून! (japun!). Warning signs say सावधान (saavdhaan).

no_problem.note: Very common in speech: काही प्रॉब्लेम नाही (kaahi problem naahi).

of_course.note: More formal: अर्थात (arthaat). Also: हो, नक्की (ho, nakki).

i_like_it.note: For a lasting liking: मला हे आवडतं (mala he aavadta).

dont_like_it.note: For a lasting dislike: मला हे आवडत नाही (mala he aavadat naahi).

im_tired.note: A woman says: मी दमले आहे (mi damle aahe). Also common: थकलो / थकले (thaklo / thakle).

im_happy.note: Also: मला खूप आनंद झाला (mala khoop aanand jhaala), 'I'm delighted'.

welcome.note: Warm and usual at the door. Formal, for events and signs: स्वागत आहे (swaagat aahe).
